Definition: from G1 (as a negative particle) and G3129; ignorant:--unlearned.
BiblicalUsage: Once, in Peter's warning about Paul's letters: As also in all his epistles, speaking in them of these things; in which are some things hard to be understood, which they that are unlearned and unstable wrest, as they do also the other scriptures, unto their own destruction. The word is unlearned, and Peter puts it beside unstable, the two marks of the man who twists the Scriptures.
TheologicalSignificance: One word for unlearned carries no doctrine of its own; its weight is the warning, that hard sayings are not to be wrested by the untaught, and the twisting ends in destruction.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
